items.title: ms_env
items.text:
ms_env gives a MolSuite app the external tools it needs: it finds one that already works, or installs it, on this machine or on a host reached over ssh. It is the lowest layer of MolSuite and uses the standard library only.

A recipe says how to tell that a tool works and how to install it. A host says where. ms_env applies one to the other.

items.title: Install
items.text:
pip install ms_env

The package requires Python 3.12 or newer. This machine may be Linux, macOS or Windows; a remote host is a POSIX machine.

items.title: First use
items.text:
from ms_env import READY, Host, ToolSpec, ensure, locate

spec = ToolSpec.load("openbabel.toml")

recipe = spec.recipe("/home/me/.myapp/tools")      # bound to this machine
state, executable = locate(recipe)                  # (READY, ".../bin/obabel") or (MISSING, "")
if state != READY:
    install = ensure(recipe)                        # returns at once: a daemon thread installs
    install.future.result()                         # wait; `install.lines` is the live log

cluster = Host("me@login.hpc")                    # as `ssh` knows it
ensure(spec.recipe("/home/me/.myapp/tools"), cluster).future.result()

@classmethod
def load(cls, path: Path | str) -> "ToolSpec":
    data = tomllib.loads(Path(path).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    tool, locate, env = data["tool"], data["locate"], data.get("env", {})
    return cls(
        name=str(tool["name"]),
        version=str(tool.get("version", "")),
        info=dict(tool),
        prefix=str(tool.get("prefix", "{tools_home}/{name}/{version}")),
        paths=tuple(locate.get("paths", ())),
        commands=tuple(locate.get("commands", ())),
        check=tuple(locate.get("check", ())),
        conda=tuple(env.get("conda", ())),
        pip=tuple(env.get("pip", ())),
        channels=tuple(env.get("channels", ("conda-forge",))),
        steps=tuple(map(_install_step, data.get("install", ()))),
    )

items.title: recipe
items.text:
recipe(tools_home: str, *, prefix: str = '', extra_paths: Iterable[str] = (), manager: str = '', platform: str = '') -> Recipe

Bind the templates to one host. tools_home/prefix are paths on that host.

prefix is a location the user chose instead of the managed one: an environment of their own (checked, never changed) or a place to install into. extra_paths are user-registered executables; manager is a conda-type program to use there instead of micromamba. platform is the host's (Host.platform()); this machine's by default.

Source code in src/ms_env/recipes.py 
def recipe(
    self,
    tools_home: str,
    *,
    prefix: str = "",
    extra_paths: Iterable[str] = (),
    manager: str = "",
    platform: str = "",
) -> Recipe:
    """Bind the templates to one host. ``tools_home``/``prefix`` are paths *on that host*.

    ``prefix`` is a location the user chose instead of the managed one: an environment of
    their own (checked, never changed) or a place to install into. ``extra_paths`` are
    user-registered executables; ``manager`` is a conda-type program to use there instead
    of micromamba. ``platform`` is the host's (``Host.platform()``); this machine's by default.
    """
    platform = platform or LOCAL.platform()
    values = {"tools_home": str(tools_home).rstrip("/\\"), "name": self.name, "version": self.version,
              "exe": "{exe}", "platform": platform}
    values["prefix"] = prefix = str(prefix or self.prefix.format_map(values)).rstrip("/\\")
    win = platform.startswith("win")
    values["bin"], values["python"] = (f"{prefix}/Library/bin", f"{prefix}/python.exe") if win else \
        (f"{prefix}/bin", f"{prefix}/bin/python")
    fill = lambda items: tuple(str(item).format_map(values) for item in items)  # noqa: E731
    steps = _env_steps(self.name, fill(self.conda), fill(self.pip), fill(self.channels), values, manager)
    unsupported = ""
    for step in self.steps:
        if not step.downloads:
            steps.append(RecipeStep(step.name, fill(step.argv), step.timeout))
            continue
        build = next(((url, sha) for where, url, sha in step.downloads if where in ("", platform)), None)
        if build is None:
            unsupported = f"{self.name} has no build for {platform}"
            continue
        steps.append(RecipeStep(step.name, (), step.timeout, url=build[0], sha256=build[1], to=fill([step.to])[0]))
    # Downloads are out of the repr of a step, so a recipe without any keeps the stamp it had.
    downloads = tuple((step.to, step.downloads) for step in self.steps if step.downloads)
    material = (self.name, self.version, self.conda, self.pip, self.channels, self.steps)
    return Recipe(
        name=self.name,
        prefix=values["prefix"],
        candidates=(*map(str, extra_paths), *fill(self.paths)),
        commands=self.commands,
        check=fill(self.check),
        steps=tuple(steps),
        conda=fill(self.conda),
        pip=fill(self.pip),
        stamp=hashlib.sha256(repr(material + ((downloads,) if downloads else ())).encode()).hexdigest()[:16],
        platform=platform,
        unsupported=unsupported,
    )

def argv(self, command: str) -> list[str]:
    """What to execute here for `sh` to run `command` there. This machine needs an `sh` for
    that, which Windows lacks: what ms_env does here it does in Python, not through this."""
    return ["sh", "-c", command] if self.address is None else [*self.ssh, self.address, command]

What command printed there, given data (bytes, or an open file) to read.

Source code in src/ms_env/host.py 
def run(self, command: str, data=b"", timeout: float = 600) -> bytes:
    """What `command` printed there, given `data` (bytes, or an open file) to read."""
    feed = {"input": data} if isinstance(data, bytes) else {"stdin": data}
    done = subprocess.run(self.argv(command), **feed, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
                          timeout=timeout)
    if done.returncode:
        said = done.stderr.decode(errors="replace").strip()
        if "Permission denied" in said:  # BatchMode: ssh does not ask, and here nobody could answer
            said += f"\nssh has to log in to {self.address} with a key, without asking: see ssh-copy-id"
        if "Host key verification failed" in said:  # the same: nobody here to say yes to a new key
            said += f"\nssh does not know {self.address} yet: log in to it once by hand (`ssh {self.address}`)"
        raise HostError(f"`{command[:200]}` on {self.address or 'this machine'}: {said or done.returncode}")
    return done.stdout

def home(self) -> str:
    """The home of the account there: where a path of ours on that machine starts."""
    if self.address is None:
        return str(Path.home())
    return self.run('printf %s "$HOME"', timeout=60).decode()

def platform(self) -> str:
    """The platform there, as conda names it (see `conda_platform`)."""
    if self.address is None:
        return conda_platform(_platform.system(), _platform.machine())
    return conda_platform(*self.run("uname -sm", timeout=60).decode().split()[:2])

items.title: app_recipe
items.text:
app_recipe(name: str, requirements: Iterable[str], imports: Iterable[str], *, prefix: str, tools_home: str, cache: Path | str, manager: str = '') -> Recipe

The recipe that gives a host the environment requirements run in here.

requirements are the packages of the app, each name or name[extras]: one imported from a source checkout goes as a wheel of its code as it is now, one that is installed is asked for in the version it has. imports are the modules that have to import there for the environment to count as usable. prefix and tools_home are paths on the host (see Host.home); cache is a directory of this machine for the wheels.

The environment is updated where it stands for as long as the Python is the same. Builds wheels the first time, and after the code changes: keep it off UI threads.

Source code in src/ms_env/app.py 
def app_recipe(
    name: str,
    requirements: Iterable[str],
    imports: Iterable[str],
    *,
    prefix: str,
    tools_home: str,
    cache: Path | str,
    manager: str = "",
) -> Recipe:
    """The recipe that gives a host the environment `requirements` run in here.

    `requirements` are the packages of the app, each `name` or `name[extras]`: one imported
    from a source checkout goes as a wheel of its code as it is now, one that is installed is
    asked for in the version it has. `imports` are the modules that have to import there for
    the environment to count as usable. `prefix` and `tools_home` are paths on the host (see
    `Host.home`); `cache` is a directory of this machine for the wheels.

    The environment is updated where it stands for as long as the Python is the same. Builds
    wheels the first time, and after the code changes: keep it off UI threads.
    """
    prefix, cache = str(prefix).rstrip("/"), Path(cache)
    code, wheels, wanted, tags = f"{prefix}/{_CODE}", [], [], []
    for requirement in requirements:
        dist, extras = re.fullmatch(r"\s*([\w.-]+)\s*(\[[^]]*])?\s*", requirement).groups()
        module = re.sub(r"[-.]+", "_", dist).lower()
        root = _checkout(module)
        if root is None:
            wanted.append(f"{dist}{extras or ''}=={metadata.version(dist)}")
            continue
        tags.append(_tree_hash(root, module))
        wheels.append(_wheel(root, tags[-1], cache))
        wanted.append(f"{code}/{wheels[-1].name}{extras or ''}")
    cache.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    constraints, loose = cache / "constraints.txt", cache / "constraints-pip.txt"
    everything, by_pip = _constraints()
    constraints.write_text(everything, encoding="utf-8")
    loose.write_text(by_pip, encoding="utf-8")

    pip = (f"{prefix}/bin/python", "-m", "pip", "install", "--progress-bar", "off")
    # ponytail: one version the index lacks drops every pin of what conda installed here, not
    # just that one. Drop them one by one if a host ever ends up too far from this environment.
    pinned = (
        'pip() { "$0" -m pip install --progress-bar off --constraint "$1" "${@:2}"; }; d=$1; shift; '
        'pip "$d/constraints.txt" "$@" || '
        '{ echo "not every version here can be had there: pinning what pip installed only"; '
        'pip "$d/constraints-pip.txt" "$@"; }'
    )
    refresh = [
        RecipeStep(
            f"send the code of {name}",
            ("sh", "-c", 'rm -rf "$0" && mkdir -p "$0" && tar -x -C "$0"', code),
            600.0,
            send=(str(constraints), str(loose), *map(str, wheels)),
        ),
        RecipeStep(
            f"install {name} and what it needs",
            ("bash", "-c", pinned, f"{prefix}/bin/python", code, *wanted),
            3600.0,
        ),
    ]
    if wheels:  # the version of a checkout does not change with its code: pip would keep the old one
        refresh.append(
            RecipeStep(
                f"install the code of {name} as it is here",
                (*pip, "--no-deps", "--force-reinstall", *(f"{code}/{wheel.name}" for wheel in wheels)),
                600.0,
            )
        )
    conda = (f"python={platform.python_version()}", "pip")
    values = {"prefix": prefix, "tools_home": str(tools_home).rstrip("/")}
    short = lambda *parts: hashlib.sha256(repr(parts).encode()).hexdigest()[:16]  # noqa: E731
    return Recipe(
        name=name,
        prefix=prefix,
        candidates=(f"{prefix}/bin/python",),
        commands=(),
        check=("{exe}", "-c", "import " + ", ".join(imports)),
        steps=(*_env_steps(name, conda, (), ("conda-forge",), values, manager), *refresh),
        conda=conda,
        stamp=short(conda, wanted, tags, constraints.read_text(encoding="utf-8")),
        refresh=tuple(refresh),
        base=short(conda),
    )

items.title: ensure
items.text:
ensure(recipe: Recipe, host: Host = LOCAL, busy: Callable[[], str] | None = None) -> Install

Make sure the tool is there: start installing it, or join the install already running.

Returns at once: wait on future and read lines for the log. Nothing is installed where the tool is already usable. An install of ours made from another recipe is made again, or brought up to this one where it stands when the recipe says how (that is the update); an environment of the user is verified and left as it is.

busy is asked only before an install of ours is changed: what it returns is why that cannot be done now (something is running from it), and the install fails saying so.

Source code in src/ms_env/recipes.py 
def ensure(recipe: Recipe, host: Host = LOCAL, busy: Callable[[], str] | None = None) -> Install:
    """Make sure the tool is there: start installing it, or join the install already running.

    Returns at once: wait on ``future`` and read ``lines`` for the log. Nothing is installed
    where the tool is already usable. An install of ours made from another recipe is made
    again, or brought up to this one where it stands when the recipe says how (that is the
    update); an environment of the user is verified and left as it is.

    ``busy`` is asked only before an install of ours is changed: what it returns is why that
    cannot be done now (something is running from it), and the install fails saying so.
    """
    key = f"{recipe.name}@{host.address or 'local'}"
    with _LOCK:
        current = _INSTALLS.get(key)
        if current is not None and not current.future.done():
            return current
        install = _INSTALLS[key] = Install(key)
    # ponytail: one daemon thread per install; a pool if installs pile up.
    # Daemon on purpose: quitting the app must not wait 30 min for a conda solve.
    threading.Thread(target=_run_install, args=(install, recipe, host, busy), name=f"ms_env-{key}", daemon=True).start()
    return install

def locate(recipe: Recipe, host: Host = LOCAL, timeout: float = 60.0) -> tuple[str, str]:
    """(READY, executable) or (MISSING | UNREACHABLE, ""). Blocks on a subprocess: keep it off UI threads.

    A candidate counts when it is there and its check passes; on Windows, `path.exe` for `path`.
    """
    if host.address is None:
        return _locate_here(recipe, timeout)
    try:
        result = subprocess.run(
            host.argv(_locate_script(recipe)),
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            timeout=timeout,
            check=False,
        )
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        return (UNREACHABLE if host.address else MISSING), ""
    found = result.stdout.strip().splitlines()
    if result.returncode == 0 and found:
        return READY, found[-1]
    return (UNREACHABLE if host.address and result.returncode == _SSH_CONNECT_FAILED else MISSING), ""

items.title: recipe_steps
items.text:
recipe_steps(recipe: Recipe, host: Host = LOCAL, refresh: bool = False) -> list[Step]

The whole install: clear what ms_env left at the prefix, run the recipe, stamp it.

The first step fails on a prefix that holds something ms_env did not install. With refresh the prefix stays and only recipe.refresh runs before the stamp.

Source code in src/ms_env/recipes.py 
def recipe_steps(recipe: Recipe, host: Host = LOCAL, refresh: bool = False) -> list[Step]:
    """The whole install: clear what ms_env left at the prefix, run the recipe, stamp it.

    The first step fails on a prefix that holds something ms_env did not install. With
    `refresh` the prefix stays and only `recipe.refresh` runs before the stamp.
    """
    label, prefix = (f"{host.address}: " if host.address else ""), _prefix(recipe)
    if recipe.unsupported and not refresh:
        raise StepFailed(recipe.unsupported)
    clear = (
        f'p={prefix}\n'
        f'if [ -n "$(ls -A "$p" 2>/dev/null)" ] && [ ! -f "$p/{STAMP}" ] && [ ! -f "$p{_INSTALLING}" ]; then\n'
        '  echo "$p holds an environment ms_env did not install: it is checked, never changed." >&2; exit 1\n'
        "fi\n"
        f'mkdir -p "$(dirname "$p")" && : > "$p{_INSTALLING}" && rm -rf -- "$p"'
    )
    stamp = (
        f'p={prefix}\nmkdir -p "$p" && printf %s {shlex.quote(_stamp_text(recipe))} > "$p/{STAMP}" '
        f'&& rm -f "$p{_INSTALLING}"'
    )
    steps = (
        *(recipe.refresh if refresh else (
            RecipeStep(f"prepare {recipe.prefix}", ("sh", "-c", clear), 300.0, local=partial(_clear_here, recipe)),
            *recipe.steps,
        )),
        RecipeStep(f"record the {recipe.name} install", ("sh", "-c", stamp), 60.0, local=partial(_stamp_here, recipe)),
    )
    return [_step(step, label, host) for step in steps]

items.text:
remove(recipe: Recipe, host: Host = LOCAL) -> bool

Delete the prefix when ms_env installed it. False: nothing of ours there, nothing deleted.

Source code in src/ms_env/recipes.py 
def remove(recipe: Recipe, host: Host = LOCAL) -> bool:
    """Delete the prefix when ms_env installed it. False: nothing of ours there, nothing deleted."""
    key = f"{recipe.name}@{host.address or 'local'}"
    with _LOCK:
        current = _INSTALLS.get(key)
        if current is not None and not current.future.done():
            raise RuntimeError(f"{recipe.name} is being installed on {host.address or 'this machine'}.")
    if host.address is None:
        _prefix(recipe)
        if not (Path(recipe.prefix, STAMP).is_file() or Path(recipe.prefix + _INSTALLING).is_file()):
            return False
        _delete(recipe.prefix, recipe.prefix + _INSTALLING)
        return True
    script = (
        f'p={_prefix(recipe)}\n[ -f "$p/{STAMP}" ] || [ -f "$p{_INSTALLING}" ] || {{ echo no; exit 0; }}\n'
        f'rm -rf -- "$p" "$p{_INSTALLING}"'
    )
    return host.run(script, timeout=600).decode().strip() != "no"

    """What the environment at the recipe's prefix lacks of what the recipe asks for; [] when it meets it.

    The way to take an environment the user already has instead of installing one: every
    pinned conda package (looked up in `conda-meta`), every pinned pip package (asked to the
    python of the prefix) and the recipe's check on the executables of that prefix. Reads
    only. ponytail: a pip URL or path is not looked up, and `>=` counts as "is there".
    """
    conda = []
    for name, version in map(_pin, recipe.conda):
        # conda's `=1.2` takes 1.2 and 1.2.x; a file there is name-version-build.json
        globs = [f"{name}-{version}-*.json", f"{name}-{version}.*-*.json"] if version else [f"{name}-[0-9]*-*.json"]
        conda.append((globs, f"conda: {name}{'=' + version if version else ''} is asked for and is not there"))
    pins = ["==".join(filter(None, _pin(spec))) for spec in recipe.pip if "/" not in spec]
    lacks = (_lacks_here if host.address is None else partial(_lacks_there, host=host))(recipe, conda, pins)
    inside = tuple(path for path in recipe.candidates if path.startswith(recipe.prefix + "/"))
    if recipe.check and status(dataclasses.replace(recipe, candidates=inside, commands=()), host) != READY:
        lacks.append(f"check: `{shlex.join(recipe.check)}` passes for none of {', '.join(inside) or 'its executables'}")
    return lacks

items.title: find_environment_manager
items.text:
find_environment_manager(*extra_variables: str) -> Path | None

The program that creates environments here: micromamba, unless a variable names another.

extra_variables are app-specific overrides, read before MOLSUITE_ENV_MANAGER; any of them may name a conda or a mamba. None: the recipe downloads its own micromamba.

Source code in src/ms_env/steps.py 
def find_environment_manager(*extra_variables: str) -> Path | None:
    """The program that creates environments here: micromamba, unless a variable names another.

    ``extra_variables`` are app-specific overrides, read before ``MOLSUITE_ENV_MANAGER``; any
    of them may name a conda or a mamba. None: the recipe downloads its own micromamba.
    """
    named = [str(os.environ.get(variable) or "").strip() for variable in (*extra_variables, "MOLSUITE_ENV_MANAGER")]
    for candidate in (*filter(None, named), shutil.which("micromamba")):
        path = Path(candidate or "").expanduser()
        if path.is_file() and os.access(path, os.X_OK):
            return path.resolve()
    return None

items.title: run_step
items.text:
run_step(step: Step, on_line: Callable[[str], None] | None = None) -> None

Run one step, streaming its output. Raises StepFailed on failure.

Source code in src/ms_env/steps.py 
def run_step(step: Step, on_line: Callable[[str], None] | None = None) -> None:
    """Run one step, streaming its output. Raises StepFailed on failure."""
    emit = on_line or (lambda _line: None)
    if step.run is not None:
        step.run(emit)
        return
    if step.call is not None:
        message = step.call()
        if message:
            emit(message)
        return
    if not step.argv:
        return
    emit("$ " + " ".join(step.argv))
    try:
        process = subprocess.Popen(
            step.argv,
            stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
            stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
            text=True,
            encoding="utf-8",  # not the locale's: cp1252 on Windows
            errors="replace",
            bufsize=1,
        )
    except FileNotFoundError as exc:
        raise StepFailed(f"{step.name}: command not found ({exc.filename}).") from exc
    deadline = time.monotonic() + step.timeout
    assert process.stdout is not None
    for line in process.stdout:
        emit(line.rstrip())
        if time.monotonic() > deadline:
            process.kill()
            raise StepFailed(f"{step.name}: timed out after {step.timeout:.0f}s.")
    try:
        code = process.wait(timeout=max(1.0, deadline - time.monotonic()))
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        process.kill()
        raise StepFailed(f"{step.name}: timed out after {step.timeout:.0f}s.") from None
    if code != 0:
        raise StepFailed(f"{step.name}: exited with code {code}.")

items.title: run_steps
items.text:
run_steps(steps: Iterable[Step], on_line: Callable[[str], None] | None = None, on_step: Callable[[int, Step], None] | None = None) -> None
Source code in src/ms_env/steps.py 
def run_steps(
    steps: Iterable[Step],
    on_line: Callable[[str], None] | None = None,
    on_step: Callable[[int, Step], None] | None = None,
) -> None:
    for index, step in enumerate(steps):
        if on_step is not None:
            on_step(index, step)
        run_step(step, on_line)

def conda_platform(system: str, machine: str) -> str:
    """`linux-64`, `osx-arm64`, `win-64`...; `system-machine` for one conda has no name for."""
    system, machine = system.lower(), machine.lower()
    return _PLATFORMS.get((system, machine), f"{system}-{machine}")

items.title: A recipe
items.text:
An app ships one TOML file per tool. Every section but [tool] and [locate] is optional.

[tool]
name = "openbabel"
label = "OpenBabel"
version = "3.1.1"                         # pinned here; never a user option
prefix = "{tools_home}/{name}/{version}"  # the default

[locate]
paths = ["{bin}/obabel"]                  # where the install puts it; +".exe" on Windows
commands = ["obabel"]                     # looked up on PATH
check = ["{exe}", "-V"]                   # {exe} = the candidate; none: being there is enough

[env]                                     # a conda prefix at {prefix}
conda = ["openbabel={version}"]
pip = []
channels = ["conda-forge"]                # the default

[[install]]                               # plain steps, after [env]
name = "fetch the weights"
argv = ["{python}", "-m", "tool.fetch", "{prefix}/weights"]
timeout = 1800

[[install]]                               # a download, checked, per platform
name = "download the binary"
to = "{prefix}/tool"                      # an archive is unpacked into `to`; a file keeps ".exe"
download.linux-64 = { url = "https://.../tool_linux", sha256 = "..." }
download.win-64 = { url = "https://.../tool.exe", sha256 = "..." }
# the same file everywhere: download = { url = "...", sha256 = "..." }

{bin} and {python} are where a conda environment keeps them: {prefix}/bin and {prefix}/bin/python, or {prefix}/Library/bin and {prefix}/python.exe on Windows. Platforms are named as conda names them (linux-64, linux-aarch64, osx-64, osx-arm64, win-64; Host.platform() says the host's). A download needs its sha256. On a platform none of its downloads names, the tool has no build: recipe.unsupported says so and ensure fails with it. A remote host gets a download made and checked here, then sent over ssh: it needs no curl.

ToolSpec.load(path) reads the file, and spec.recipe(tools_home) binds its templates to one host. tools_home is a path on that host.

from ms_env import ToolSpec

spec = ToolSpec.load("openbabel.toml")
recipe = spec.recipe("/home/me/.myapp/tools")

recipe() takes three more choices of the user:

Argument What it is prefix= A location in place of the managed one: an environment of their own, or a place to install into extra_paths= Executables the user registered, tried before anything else manager= A conda-type program to use on the host in place of micromamba platform= The host's platform (Host.platform()); this machine's by default

items.title: Finding a tool
items.text:
locate(recipe, host) returns (READY, executable), or (MISSING, ""), or (UNREACHABLE, "") when ssh could not connect. status returns the state alone. The first candidate whose check exits 0 wins, in this order:

  1. The paths the user registered.
  2. The managed install under tools_home.
  3. The commands on PATH.

Both calls block on a subprocess, so keep them off UI threads.

items.title: Installing a tool
items.text:
ensure(recipe, host) returns an Install at once and installs on a daemon thread. Nothing is installed where the tool is already usable.

from ms_env import ensure

install = ensure(recipe)
install.future.result()     # waits; raises when the install failed
print(*install.lines, sep="\n")
  • install.lines is the live log, and its last line is the error when there is one.
  • A second ensure of the same tool on the same host joins the install that is running.
  • [env] is created with micromamba: the one on the host's PATH, or one downloaded into tools_home.

An app that shows the steps itself takes them from recipe_steps(recipe, host) and runs them with run_steps(steps, on_line, on_step).

items.title: Whose an environment is
items.text:
ensure stamps the prefix it installs. The stamp decides what may happen to it:

At the prefix ensure remove Nothing Creates it Nothing to delete A stamp of this recipe Nothing Deletes it A stamp of another recipe (the TOML changed) Creates it again: the update Deletes it Something without a stamp: the user's own environment Verifies it, never changes it Leaves it 
from ms_env import remove, verify

mine = spec.recipe("/home/me/.myapp/tools", prefix="/home/me/envs/babel")   # an environment I already have
verify(mine)    # [] when it meets the recipe, else what it lacks:
                # ["conda: openbabel=3.1.1 is asked for and is not there"]
remove(recipe)  # True: ms_env had installed it and it is gone

verify looks up every pinned conda package, every pinned pip package and the recipe's check, and only reads. An executable registered on its own (extra_paths=) is not an environment: it only has to pass the check.

items.title: While something runs from it
items.text:
An update replaces an install, so an app can refuse it while the install is in use. ensure takes busy=, a function that returns why the install cannot be changed now, or an empty string.

ensure(recipe, host, busy=lambda: "2 jobs are running from it")

busy is asked only before an install of ms_env is changed. When it returns a reason the install fails saying so and the prefix is left as it is. A prefix that is missing, or already as the recipe asks, never asks.

items.title: A host
items.text:
Host() is this machine. Host("me@login.hpc") runs every command through the system's ssh with BatchMode=yes:

  • Users, keys and jumps come from ~/.ssh/config.
  • The key logs in or the command fails at once; no credential is handled.
  • Nothing is left listening on the other side.
from ms_env import Host

host = Host("me@login.hpc")
home = host.home()                  # the home of the account there
host.run("nproc").decode()          # what the command printed; HostError when it fails

A failed login says what to do: ssh-copy-id when the key is not accepted, a first login by hand when the host key is not known yet.

items.title: The environment of an app
items.text:
app_recipe makes the recipe that gives a host the environment an app runs in here: the same Python and the same versions of what this one has installed.

from ms_env import Host, app_recipe, ensure

host = Host("me@login.hpc")
home = host.home()
recipe = app_recipe(
    "myapp",
    ["myapp", "ms_flow"],                     # packages: `name` or `name[extras]`
    ["myapp", "ms_flow"],                     # modules that have to import there
    prefix=f"{home}/.myapp/env",              # on the host
    tools_home=f"{home}/.myapp/tools",        # on the host
    cache="/home/me/.myapp/cache/wheels",     # on this machine
)
ensure(recipe, host).future.result()

What travels and what is downloaded:

  • A package imported from a source checkout goes as a wheel of its code as it is now. The wheel is built once for each state of the code and of its last tag, where its version comes from. A checkout that lacks the tag of a release made on the server builds a development version below it, which the host refuses for an app that asks for that release: git fetch --tags in it.
  • A package that is installed here is asked for in the version it has.
  • Everything else the host downloads, pinned to the versions of this environment, so the two machines may be different systems.
  • When an index lacks a version that conda installed here, the install tries again pinning only what pip installed.

The environment is updated where it stands for as long as the Python version is the same; a new Python makes it again. app_recipe builds wheels the first time and after the code changes, so keep it off UI threads.

items.title: The environment manager
items.text:
find_environment_manager() returns the program that creates environments on this machine, or None when a recipe has to download its own micromamba.

  1. The variables the app names, in the order given.
  2. MOLSUITE_ENV_MANAGER.
  3. micromamba on PATH.

Any of the variables may name a conda or a mamba.
